content.thinking:
I'm writing up the postmortem now, starting from the key facts: the alert fired on a drop in the confidence ratio with no rise in errors. The deploy at 02:05:10 switched the categoriser model from v1 to v2, and the rollback is confirmed.

I'm weighing how to word the symptom for the postmortem: the record only shows the share of purchases categorised confidently dropped, so I'm leaning toward saying fewer purchases were confidently filed under a category rather than claiming a specific wrong filing I can't verify.

I'm working out the causal chain for the postmortem, starting with the symptom: the shop stopped confidently categorising many purchases. Next I'm tracing why, tying the v2 model at production back to the 02:05:10 deploy, and checking whether the earlier deploy has been ruled out.

I'm checking whether the earlier deploy can be ruled out: the metrics from about 20:10 to 02:11 show the service healthy with that revision in place, and no flag changes came from anyone but Argus in the hour before onset. The rollback restored the earlier revision and was confirmed, so I'm citing that row for the fix.

I'm working out the root cause now: the v2 model looks words up exactly as they come in, and its vocabulary is lowercase, while the serving path passes titles through without lowercasing. Capitalised words therefore miss the vocabulary and fall to "General" without confidence, which is what v1 avoided by lowercasing inside predict. I'm noting that this comes from the code-fix reading of main rather than the deployed revision, so it is not yet confirmed as the running behaviour.

I'm settling on how to word the cause: the new model expects lowercase words, and the shop was not lowercasing titles before handing them over, so I'll say that this likely left capitalised words unrecognised. Next I'm checking whether the faulty path is still live, since the repository still sets the categoriser to v2, so turning automatic sync back on or redeploying could bring the same problem back.

I'm checking the contributing factors now. The first one is that the v2 tests only used lowercase words, so a mismatch on capitalised titles would have slipped through before the change shipped. I'm considering whether the item that adds the new test actually covers that gap, or only the fault's own tests.

I'm checking the other contributing factor now: no staged check was seen comparing the new model's categorisation against the old one before the config change went out. I'm considering whether a comparison on real purchase titles before release would close that gap, and whether anything in the record shows a staged rollout.

I'm now weighing how to write up the contributing factors: one is that no check was run on the new model's output against the old before the change went out, and I'm considering whether an action item that adds that check would cover it, since the fix's own test wouldn't.

I'm now weighing a second contributing factor: the change reached the production replicas without any staged rollout that I can see in the record. Whether it was staged is unknown, so I won't assume either way, but a canary would have limited the affected purchases, so I'll propose one as an action item.

I'm drafting the action items now: a pre-release check that compares a model switch's confident share against the current model on real purchase titles, a staged rollout for categoriser model changes, and routing the low-confidence alert to on-call paging so someone is told. I'm also considering a mitigation item to set the categoriser back to v1 in the production values until a deploy carrying the fix has gone out.

I'm sorting the lessons into what went well, what went wrong, and what was lucky. Argus's rollback and the confirmed mitigation go under what went well, along with tying the onset to the deploy diff and the draft fix from Code-Fix. Nobody being paged is the main thing that went wrong, so that goes in its own list.

I'm checking what the record can and can't support here: the config change is the only difference shown in the deploy diff, but I haven't compared either revision directly against main. I'm also taking the confidence series as a fair picture of what shoppers see, and I'll keep figures out of the write-up and refer to the replicas as all of them.

I'm laying out the next part of the postmortem: the symptom first, as shoppers' purchases no longer being confidently categorised while failed requests stayed within normal variation. Then the cause, that the production categoriser was switched from v1 to v2 by the deploy at the onset, with all replicas running that revision by the time of the read. I'm also checking the earlier deploy, which the metrics from before it through to the onset appear to rule out.

I'm checking the earlier deploy against the metrics: the read reaches back before it and shows the service healthy until the onset, and rolling back to its revision returned things to normal. I'm also noting that no flag changes came from anyone but Argus in the hour before onset.

Now I'm working out the root cause: model v2 probably missed capitalised words in purchase titles, since it looks words up exactly as given against a lowercased vocabulary, and the categoriser passes titles through without lowercasing them.

I'm pinning down the root cause as the mechanism: under v2, words in purchase titles that weren't already lowercase likely stopped matching the model's vocabulary, so those purchases fell to General without confidence. The categoriser file is unchanged between the two revisions, so the difference has to be in the config switch itself.

I'm checking the lessons list now, with the rollback and the confirmed mitigation under what went well, and I'll keep the paging gap as the one thing that went wrong.

action_items.item: Add a pre-release check for categoriser model changes: run the candidate model over a sample of real, mixed-case purchase titles and block the change if its confident share falls below the current model's.
Roll out categoriser model changes to part of the replicas first, and go on only if the confident-categorisation share holds.
Set categoriser.model back to v1 in deploy/values-production.yaml until a deploy carrying the fix from PR #567 has gone out, so the repository says what should run.
Route CategorisationConfidenceLow alerts on io-shop to the on-call rota so a person is paged.

causal_chain.step: Many shoppers' purchases were no longer filed confidently under a category, while failed requests stayed within their normal variation.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy P1 of revision d268103129978816ce705c50c14cd42c7c5fe46e. The metrics read reach back before it and show the service healthy until the onset at {T6.2}, and rolling back to that revision was confirmed to bring the service back to normal.
A feature flag change. The flag provider's history showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before the investigation, and the flag read before the onset returned none.

causal_chain.step: The production categoriser had been switched from model v1 to model v2. Deploy P2 at {P2.1} changed categoriser.model in deploy/values-production.yaml from v1 to v2. That is the only file the diff D1 lists, and S1 shows v2 set at the running revision. As of {T10.1}, all {T10.2} replicas ran that revision, and rolling the service back off it put things right (M1).
Under v2, purchase titles with capitalised words likely stopped matching the model's vocabulary, so those purchases fell to the general category without a confident filing.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching the shop to a newer model for sorting purchases into categories likely left capitalised words in product titles unrecognised: the new model only knows lowercase words, and the shop passed titles on without lowercasing them.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that runs a new categoriser model against mixed-case purchase titles and compares its confident share with the current model's before the config change ships. According to Code-Fix, the existing v2 tests used only words that were already lowercase.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The v2 switch would have shown a fall in confident filings before it reached production, and would have been stopped before it went out.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The model switch went out as a plain config change to the whole deployment. No staged rollout and no gate on the confidence series were seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only some of the traffic would have been served by v2 before the fall in confidence was noticed, so fewer purchases would have been filed without confidence.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the diff of the suspect deployment, which showed the categoriser model moving from v1 to v2.
The Mitigation Agent rolled the io-shop deployment back off revision 7c3ca00c7528df68d533f6e87acd4f23a55ab342.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed the rollback, after which the alerting rule stopped firing.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #567 for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was brought in while Argus handled it.

input.root_cause: Model v2 looks words up exactly as it is given them, against a vocabulary built from titles that were already lowercased. The shop's `categorise` passes `title.split()` to `predict` without lowercasing it, a step v1 does itself inside `predict`. Under v2, any capitalised word in a purchase title missed the vocabulary, so the purchase was filed under "General" with `confident=False`. This is Code-Fix's reading of src/io_shop/categorising.py on main.
input.still_at_risk: If automatic sync is turned back on, or the service is deployed again, while the repository still sets the categoriser to v2, the new model could come back and many purchases could again be filed without a confident category.
input.symptom: The shop stopped confidently categorising many shoppers' purchases
